regions.text: ゐる。前者ばそれの反對が矛盾を含むものであり後者はそれの反勤が矛盾を含まないものである。さうして絕對的必然（absolumentnecessaire）のみが嚴密なる意味で必然であるので假説的必然（ncessaireexhypothesi），は確徴であるに過ぎないとしてゐる。

quote.translation: Leibniz, in the Discourse on Metaphysics, seeking to set up a distinction between the necessary (nécessaire) and the certain (certain), holds that the former is that whose opposite contains a contradiction and the latter that whose opposite does not, and that since only the absolutely necessary (absolument nécessaire) is necessary in the strict sense, the hypothetically necessary (nécessaire ex hypothesi) is no more than certain.

regions.text: たとへばシーザーがルビョ河で止まらずにこの河を渡つたことブフルサルスの職で敗れずに勝つたことは必然ではないが磁實である。さうして確質ではあるが必然でない故にそのことは偶然であると読いてゐる。

quote.translation: That Caesar did not stop at the Rubicon but crossed it, for example, and that he did not lose but won the battle of Pharsalus, are not necessary but certain, and because they are certain but not necessary, Leibniz explains, they are contingent.

quote.translation: The reason why something is certain and yet not necessary, that is, the reason why it is contingent, he Grounds in the will of God, which is to say in the freedom of choice (Leibniz, Discours de métaphysique, § 13).

quote.translation: Leibniz's concept of the "certain", in short, seeks to express empirical necessity, that is, metaphysical contingency.

regions.text: ともかくも系列の各成員は絶對起始によつて制約されてある限う、絶對約起始の性格を反映し、各部分は全體の部分である限う、全體の性格が投射せられてゐる。

quote.translation: At any rate, each member of the series, insofar as it is conditioned by the absolute beginning, reflects the character of the absolute beginning, and in each part, insofar as it is a part of the whole, the character of the whole is projected.

regions.text: 「必然ー偶然者」こしての絶對者の性格は各成員、各部分にあって必然し偶然者としての運命の形を取つて來る。

quote.translation: The character of the absolute as the necessary-contingent comes to take, in each member and each part, the form of fate as the necessary-contingent.

quote.translation: Kant's so-called "lawfulness of the contingent" (Gesetzlichkeit des Zufälligen), that is, the concept of purposiveness (Kant, Kritik der Urteils- kraft, § 76), is likewise nothing other than the necessary-contingent character possessed by a part determined by the whole.
